questions.question: Relative humidity expresses:
options: The vapour actually present as a percentage of the maximum that air at that temperature could carry
The mass of vapour per cubic metre in grams
The temperature at which frost forms

questions.question: Air at 25 °C can carry a maximum of 23 g/m³ and actually holds 11,5 g/m³. Its relative humidity is:
That same parcel is cooled to about 13 °C, where its ceiling is 11,5 g/m³. Without any water being added it is now:
options: SATURATED — 100% relative humidity, because the capacity collapsed around the unchanged moisture

questions.question: When both air temperature and dew point are known, the most useful reading is:
options: The GAP between them — small gap means near-saturation, wide gap means dry air

subtopics.title: Condensation — From Dew to the Condensation Level

questions.question: Frost forms instead of dew when:
options: The dew point lies below freezing, so vapour fixes directly onto surfaces as ice
The night is cloudy and windy

questions.question: The grey wall of fog that drifts over Saldanha and the West Coast villages is ADVECTION fog because:
options: It forms in valley floors overnight
Moist ocean air moves horizontally across the cold Benguela water and is chilled below its dew point
It is smoke from fishing boats

questions.question: A rising parcel of air cools adiabatically because:
options: Falling pressure lets it expand, and expansion itself lowers its temperature — no heat is removed

questions.question: Surface temperature 28 °C, dew point 16 °C, dry adiabatic lapse rate 1 °C per 100 m. The condensation level lies at:
options: 1 200 m — the parcel must shed 12 degrees at 1 degree per 100 metres

subtopics.title: Clouds — Naming Them and Reading Their Weather

questions.question: The name-part NIMBUS tells you the cloud is:
A pale milky veil of high ice-crystal cloud with a luminous ring around the sun is:
options: CIRROSTRATUS — its halo is a classic sign of rain within a day or two

questions.question: Long, steady, soaking rain through a dark shapeless sky comes from:
options: NIMBOSTRATUS — the thick low layer cloud, unlike the brief showers of a cumulonimbus

questions.question: A cumulonimbus spreads into an anvil at its top because:
options: Wind blows only at the top
The stable stratosphere refuses it entry, so the rising tower is forced to spread sideways at that ceiling

questions.question: The three rainfall types differ from one another only in:
options: The LIFTING mechanism that forces the air upward

questions.question: George and Knysna are green while the Klein Karoo behind the Outeniqua range is dry because the Klein Karoo:
options: Is too hot for rain to form
Lies in the RAIN SHADOW — air descending the leeward slope compresses, warms and dries

questions.question: A cloudless Free State morning that ends in a violent, localised four-o'clock thunderstorm is the signature of:
options: CONVECTIONAL rainfall — thermals off the superheated ground hoist the air kilometres upward through the day

questions.question: The Western Cape receives its rain mainly between May and August because:
options: Convection is strongest there in winter
The Agulhas Current reverses in winter
Successions of COLD FRONTS wheel in from the south-west off the Atlantic in those months, wedging warm moist air upward

questions.question: In the sponge picture of humidity:
options: Warm air is a big sponge and cold air is a small one — cooling shrinks the sponge around the water it already holds
Cold air is the bigger sponge
The sponge only fills when it rains

questions.question: Your glasses mist over when you step out of an air-conditioned mall into muggy air because:
options: The mall air follows you outside
The cold lenses chill the humid air touching them below its dew point, and the surplus moisture lands on the glass
The lenses absorb water from your skin

questions.question: The habit the section drills for weather questions is to:
options: Memorise the absolute humidity of each city
Read the DISTANCE between air temperature and dew point — a small gap means the sponge is nearly full and weather is brewing

questions.question: The four name-parts translate as:
options: Cirro high and wispy, alto middle, strato flattened sheet, cumulo heaped — with nimbus flagging rain falling now
Cirro low, alto raining, strato heaped, cumulo high
All four mean different kinds of rain
They are the names of four scientists

questions.question: Fog is best described as:
options: A completely different substance from cloud
Stratus cloud that has settled onto the ground

questions.question: Every cumulus in the sky floats on the same invisible floor because:
options: That height is the condensation level — where every rising parcel in that air mass reaches its dew point

questions.question: Farm families have long read a halo around the sun as a rain warning because it is produced by:
options: CIRROSTRATUS — the milky ice-veil that often runs a day or two ahead of a front

subtopics.title: The Ramp, the Fire and the Wedge

questions.question: 'The ramp' produces relief rainfall by:
options: Forcing wet sea air up a mountain face, where it cools, fills and tips its water on the windward side
Sliding cold air under warm air

questions.question: Rain from 'the fire' — convectional rainfall — typically:
options: Falls steadily for three days across whole provinces
Breaks in a short, violent, localised late-afternoon burst, sometimes soaking one farm and missing the next

questions.question: 'The wedge' lifts warm air because:
options: Warm air is heavier than cold air
Cold air is denser, so it slides underneath the warm moist air and levers it off the ground like a wedge under a log
The rotation of the earth spins it upward

questions.question: The trap the lesson warns against is classifying rainfall by:
options: How hard it falls — violence is not the test; the machine that lifted the air is
